context.problemStatement:
Implement the `Local` case of `lookup`. If the `name` is bound in the current
frame's `bindings`, return `Ok(value)` for the `value` to which it is bound.
Otherwise, look it up in the `parent` environment.

> **Note:** A frame's `bindings` is a `Dict(String, Value)`.
> [`dict.get(bindings, name)`](https://hexdocs.pm/gleam_stdlib/gleam/dict.html#get)
> returns `Ok(value)` if `bindings` binds `name` to `value`, and `Error(Nil)` if it
> doesn't bind `name`.

The value of every name is found this way: function parameters, `let` bindings,
names bound by `case` patterns, and global names such as `Point` and `abs`. In
this interpreter, even `+` and `*` are just built-in function names that are
looked up to access their implementations.

```
/// The value bound to name in env. A name is looked up exactly as in an
/// environment diagram: check the current frame's bindings, then its
/// parent's, and so on out to the Global frame. A name that no frame binds
/// is an errors.UnboundVariable(name) error.
pub fn lookup(env: Env, name: String) -> Result(Value, EvalError) {
  case env {
    Local(bindings, parent) ->
      // YOUR CODE HERE (replace the code below)
      Error(errors.NotImplemented(
        "lookup("
        <> name
        <> ") in Local("
        <> string.inspect(dict.keys(bindings))
        <> ", "
        <> string.inspect(parent)
        <> ")",
      ))
    Global(bindings) ->
      case mutable_dict.get(bindings, name) {
        Ok(value) -> Ok(value)
        Error(Nil) -> Error(errors.UnboundVariable(name))
      }
  }
}
```

Run the tests:

```
gleam test -- q1
```
